To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a potent and selective inhibitor of monoacylglyerol lipase (MJN110; 1–10 mg/kg) produced a robust anti‐nociception in a model of OA pain.

1) MJN110 is effective in reducing pain behaviour in the rat model of OA, 2) MJN110 reduces pain behaviours by activating spinal cannabinoid type-1 receptors, 3) MJN110 does not alter joint histopathology and 4) MJN110 produces robust anti-nociceptive effects in a model of OA pain.

MJN110, a potent and selective inhibitor of MAG lipase, attenuated mechanical allodynia and heat hyperalgesia in a rat model of OA pain, and these effects were mediated by spinal cannabinoid type 1 (CB1) and transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) receptors.
